findings.technicalRationale: The Russian origin says this CA issues host certificates, but the field is the signature on the issued SSH user certificate. The host suffix names the server-host-trust failure variant, not the certificate type. This reverses the user-CA versus host-identity distinction central to the case. Current source retains certType=user, the user-CA private key and issuance of an SSH user certificate before the later failed host-key check.

currentSourceEvidence.evidence: certType is user, not a server-host certificate; caPrivate is the protected user-CA key; caSignature origin is Computed locally with the user-CA private key.

The case issues a fresh SSH user certificate before the host-exchange; the host variant later fails expected server-host identity checking. The variant name does not change the certificate issuer into a host-certificate CA.
